samples.summary: New global focus-release contradicts the existing "dismiss must restore focus to the trigger" contract of the keepalive dropdowns used by the slides text-edit toolbar, stranding focus on <body> while the in-place text box is still mounted
samples.evidence: `font-family-picker.tsx:155-158` — `if (family === null) { // No pick — let Radix restore focus to the trigger so Esc / outside-click dismiss does not strand focus on <body>. return; }` and the identical guard in `text-paragraph-group.tsx:94-101`. Both controls are rendered inside the slides text-edit toolbar (`packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/text-edit-section.tsx:65,89`), which now sits under `data-canvas-toolbar`. The new hook only clears its `pointerDriven` flag on `Tab`, so after the user opens one of these menus with the mouse and dismisses it with Escape or an outside click, Radix restores focus to the trigger, `focusin` fires inside the toolbar, and the deferred `releaseFocusToBody()` blurs the trigger. Because these triggers carry `data-text-edit-keepalive`, the docs text-box editor deliberately skipped its commit (`packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:736-751`) and the in-place editor is still mounted — but nothing holds focus any more. Subsequent keys now target `document.body`, which is exactly what `isEditableTarget()` gates on (`packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:177,211`), so Delete/Backspace deletes the element being edited and printable keys drive canvas rules instead of typing. Fix belongs in the new hook (skip release while the editor is in text-edit mode / for `[data-text-edit-keepalive]` controls).

samples.summary: BoardToolbar reuses the same SlidesEditor keyboard gate but was not opted into the fix, so issue #882 remains reproducible on boards
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/board/board-toolbar.tsx:178` renders `<Toolbar>` with no `data-canvas-toolbar` and never calls `useCanvasFocusRelease()`, while its own header comment (lines 91-106) states it drives the reused `SlidesEditor` and reuses the slides toolbar's leaf controls off the same `getToolbarState`. Since the shortcut gate lives in `packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts` (shared by boards), every board toolbar button still parks focus on a `<button>` and silently kills arrow/Delete/z-order shortcuts.

samples.summary: Existing per-control `useMenuCloseHandlers(releaseFocusToBody)` call sites are now redundant with (and can race) the new global release
samples.evidence: `shape-controls.tsx:60`, `border-picker.tsx:72`, `text-element-controls.tsx:62`, `table-controls.tsx:103` and `fill-picker/gradient-editor.tsx:307` all already call `releaseFocusToBody()` on swatch close. With `useCanvasFocusRelease()` mounted, the same blur is now also scheduled globally on the next task; the two mechanisms overlap and the per-control ones are no longer the single source of truth for this behaviour (the diff neither removes nor documents them).

samples.summary: On mobile the hook installs three capture-phase document listeners for a toolbar root that never carries the opt-in attribute
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:70` calls `useCanvasFocusRelease()` before the `isMobile` early return at line 92, but `MobileSlidesToolbar` (`toolbar/mobile-toolbar.tsx:94`) renders no `data-canvas-toolbar` root, so the pointerdown/keydown/focusin listeners are pure overhead on every mobile slides session and the mobile sheets get no fix.

verdict.reason: Every claimed element is present as described. The new `useCanvasFocusRelease` hook (toolbar-focus-release.ts:79-106) clears `pointerDriven` only on Tab (line 87) and, on any later `focusin` inside `[data-canvas-toolbar]`, defers one task and blurs the focused, non-open-popup toolbar button (line 104). The repo's own co-located test (toolbar-focus-release.test.tsx:61-67) asserts that a pointer-opened Radix menu dismissed with Escape ends with focus on `document.body`. The slides text-edit toolbar is inside that root (`app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:110`, `useCanvasFocusRelease()` at :70), and it renders FontFamilyPicker (text-edit-section.tsx:65) and TextParagraphGroup (text-edit-section.tsx:89), whose `onCloseAutoFocus` guards explicitly rely on Radix restoring focus to the trigger on Esc/outside-click "so ... dismiss does not strand focus on <body>" (font-family-picker.tsx:154-159; text-paragraph-group.tsx:94-101). Those triggers carry `data-text-edit-keepalive` (font-family-picker.tsx:133; text-paragraph-group.tsx:82), which makes the docs in-place editor deliberately skip its commit and stay mounted (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:736-751) — and nothing re-focuses it (no activeElement watchdog anywhere in packages/). With focus on <body>, `isEditableTarget` is false (keyboard.ts:871-890) so the Delete/Backspace element-removal rule fires (keyboard.ts:214-231) via the ungated document keydown path (editor.ts:3481-3483, 2727-2729). No guard, caller, or config makes this unreachable; the hook has no keepalive/text-edit-mode exemption. This is a behaviour change to an exported hook breaking a documented contract of consumers outside the diff — in-lane and blocking.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. The board mounts the same slides editor (board-view.tsx:8,273 -> initializeEditor from @wafflebase/slides) and therefore sits behind the same document-level shortcut gate, whose isEditableTarget returns true for any focused BUTTON / role="button" (packages/slides/src/view/editor/interactions/keyboard.ts:871-889, applied at lines 131-761). The new opt-in mechanism requires BOTH a mounted useCanvasFocusRelease() and an ancestor matching [data-canvas-toolbar] (toolbar-focus-release.ts:58,67,94,104). Repo-wide greps for CANVAS_TOOLBAR_ATTR / data-canvas-toolbar / useCanvasFocusRelease / toolbar-focus-release show exactly one production consumer: packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/index.tsx:4,69-70,110. BoardToolbar renders a bare <Toolbar> (board-toolbar.tsx:178) and calls no such hook; the shared Toolbar primitive does not inject the attribute (components/ui/toolbar.tsx:11-27, props-spread only); BoardView renders BoardToolbar as an unwrapped sibling (board-view.tsx:783-812); and board-local focus code (sticky onCloseAutoFocus at board-toolbar.tsx:315-324, window blur at board-view.tsx:643) does nothing equivalent. No counterexample exists anywhere I could reach, so a pointer-driven board toolbar interaction still parks focus on a button and suppresses arrow/Delete/z-order shortcuts — the fix's sibling consumer of the shared gate was left inconsistent.
